w: Disregarding Fatigue and Hunger After a two-and-a-half hour drive from Preston, Swamishri arrived in Leicester at 12.40 pm. After Thakorji's darshan and attending the brief welcoming assembly, Swamishri saw an old devotee. Despite his long journey he went to the left of the stage, bent low without any support and enquired of his health. By the time Swamishri reached his residence it was 1.25 pm - late by 55 minutes for lunch. When Swamishri got up to have lunch he came across Thakorji's room. Thal had been offered to Thakorji (Lord Harikrishna Maharaj). On seeing Thakorji, Swamishri entered the room and without the slightest hurry, lovingly did darshan of Thakorji and the murtis in the home-mandir. Despite the 55 minute delay in his routine lunch schedule, Swamishri was patiently engaged in Thakorji's darshan.

During a special assembly of 1,500 fishermen who have become satsangis and given up their traditional occupation, Pujya Viveksagar Swami and Pujya Vivekswarup Swami talked about BAPS activities for the uplift of tribal people and fishermen (Tandels). Thereafter, kishores performed a local dance. Finally, in his address, Swamishri said, "The ocean of life is full of mundane attractions. To redeem oneself from it one needs a physical body, that is a boat. Then one requires a good navigator, that is a bona fide guru wedded to dharma, gnan, vairagya and bhakti, who can save you from the storms and obstacles in life and transport you to God. And thirdly, one requires appropriate winds, that is God's grace, to propel the boat ahead. If one has firm refuge in and devotion towards God the He will grace you...."

In the evening assembly Swamishri welcomed Pujya Mahant Rameshwardasji of Shri Jagannath Jagdish Mandir, Amdavad. The Mahant extended an invitation to Swamishri to visit the Jagannath Mandir on the eve of the Rath Yatra festival.

Thereafter, in the evening assembly, members of bal, kishore and yuvak mandals presented a drama, 'Brahmadarshan', depicting the glory of Aksharbrahma as preached by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the scriptures.
Shri Pradipbhai Kevadiya, a Hindi speaking aspirant, came with his son to Swamishri.
Pradip: "My son has passed with 88% in his tenth grade exams. Now he wishes to do further studies in the engineering faculty. But I've been telling him to go into medicine."
Swamishri asked the boy, "What is your wish?"
Boy: "I prefer to do engineering."
Pradip: "If he studies medicine then he will be able to serve society in a better way."
Swamishri: "But he desires to do engineering. If he does study medicine as you wish, then he will not be able to put his mind to it."
Pradip: "He will do whatever you say."
Swamishri: "Let him do engineering."
Then Swamishri told the boy, "I have told you to do according to your wish. Now you should do what I wish. Study properly and be obedient to your mother and father. Do puja and remember God."

Swamishri forged with care and understanding a win-win situation where he permitted the boy to do further studies according to his liking and at the same time strengthened his respect for his parents and advised him to study sincerely.

ds.t: Keep the joy of what you have attained
w: During the pradakshina of the mandir, the sadhus were singing, 'Why should we remain kangal?' "What does kangal mean?" Swamishri asked.
"Poor," said a sadhu.

Swamishri said, "In satsang we must live humbly as the poor, but keep the joy of what we have attained. What is greater than having met God and the Sant? After that do not think, 'What will become of me? I have become poor.' Do not believe that. Do not keep any of that poverty of spirit. If everything works out, it is a joy. If someone slaps us twice, it is still a joy. Honour or insult, it is still a joy."
